hero.h1: Speech to Text API for Any Audio or Video File
hero.subtitle: Send an audio or video file from your app and get punctuated text back, with each speaker labelled and each segment timestamped. Any length, any common format, over 100 languages.

quickAnswer.question: What does a speech to text API do?
quickAnswer.answer: It converts the speech in a recording into text your application can use. You upload the file; the API returns the transcript. With TranscriptX there is no file size limit, and an hour of audio comes back in about 1–2 minutes.

content: Upload caps and per-request time limits push work back onto you: compressing, splitting, stitching results together. TranscriptX has no file size limit — a voice note and a ten-hour recording go through the same request.
Video files are accepted directly, so there is no step to extract the audio first. Files already in the cloud can be sent as a Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or direct link.

content: The Web Speech API built into browsers is meant for live dictation on a web page. It does not transcribe files, label speakers or produce subtitles.
A server-side API is the right fit for recorded audio and background processing. For live captions in the browser, see [Real-Time Speech to Text](/real-time-speech-to-text).

On October 6, 2026, the TranscriptX team timed the live service: one hour of audio took 1–2 minutes (1 min 19 s at best), and a 10-hour file finished in about 10 minutes. Accuracy on clear audio was around 95%. Noise and crosstalk lower that, so test with your own recordings.

items.a: Yes. Common video formats are transcribed directly.

items.q: Can I use it as a voice to text API for memos and calls?
items.a: Yes. Voice notes, calls and dictation all work the same way. For one-off files without code, try [Voice to Text](/voice-to-text).

items.q: Do I need to set the language?
items.a: No. Over 100 languages are detected automatically.

items.q: Is my audio used to train AI?
items.a: No. Files are deleted after a few days and never used for training.

content: No size limit, no conversion, speakers and timestamps included. Working with video links instead of files? See the [Transcription API](/transcription-api).
